newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: PACIFIC HIGHWAY MAY STAY CLOSED
The Fire Brigade says the Pacific Highway could be closed all day
after a semi-trailer loaded with granulated chlorine overturned in
northern New South Wales.
The truck was also carrying other substances, and there are fears there could be problems if chemicals mix as the clean-up starts.
HERRON ASKED TO INTERVENE IN PROJECT DISPUTE
Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron, has been urged to
intervene in a dispute which is jeopardising the setting up of a
unique project aimed at stopping young Aborigines from taking up a life of crime.
The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission has refused to
provide recurrent funding for a youth revival centre on the New
South Wales far south coast.
The Bolloway Aboriginal Corporation at Batemans Bay wants to set up the centre to use traditional Koorie culture and teaching to turn
around young first offenders.
Earlier this year, ATSIC provided four-hundred-and-50-thousand
dollars to buy a property for the centre, but now won't provide any
money.
Bolloway's chairman, Les Simon, says he can't get any answers for ATSIC's change of heart.
NATIVE TITLE AGREEMENT FIRST ON MAINLAND AUSTRALIA
Members of the Dunghutti community on the New South Wales mid-north
coast, say an agreement they've signed with the State Government is long awaited recognition of their rights to land.
The Dunghutti had loged a native title claim on an area of Crown
land at Cresent Head, near Kemspey, which had been earmarked by the
State Government for residential development.
Under the agreement signed yesterday, the Government will aquire the land but pay the Dunghutti compensation and recognise them as
the native title holders.
The agreement is believed to be the first native title agreement of
its type on mainland Australia.
Mary Lou Buck says her ancestors would be proud and pleased with the agreement, which she says shows the spirit of Aboriginal
reconciliation is still alive.
KICKETT BOOTS LAST GOAL FOR SWAN
In AFL, Sydney Swans player Derek Kickett has announced his
retirement from the game.
After 152 games playing for Essendon, North Melbourne and three
seasons with the Swans, Kickett says he's decided to step aside to give younger players an opportunity.
CHINESE GROUPS ASK IF GOVT RETURNS TO WHITE AUSTRALIA POLICY
The Federal Government has been accused of returning to the White
Australia Policy with some of its immigration policies.
A letter criticising Prime Minister John Howard's failure to
denounce comments made by Independent MP Pauline Hanson in her
controversial maiden speech to parliament, will be sent to him today.
The letter, signed by more than one hundred Chinese community
groups, says Mr Howard's silence on the issue is encouraging other
people to make similar statements.
Chair of the New South Wales Ethnic Communities Council, Angela Chan, says the Government's immigration policies contradict Mr
Howard's praise of Asian immigrants in Parliament this week.
Ms Chan is particularly critical of the requirement that people who speak English will receive extra points.
DONDAS ON ANTI-EUTHANASIA BILL
The Northern Territory's Federal Member, Nick Dondas, says he's
helping to prepare an amendment to defeat the anti-voluntary
euthanasia bill in Federal parliament, before it's debated.
Kevin Andrew's bill, aimed at over-riding the Territory's voluntary euthanasia law, is due to be debated in a Federal Parliament side
chamber at the end of the month.
Mr Dondas voted in favour of having debate over the Andrews bill
moved out of the main parilamentary chamber.
He says the advantage is that it will be dealt with quickly.
Meanwhile, Mr Dondas says he's helping euthansia supporter, South
Australian M-P Chris Gallus, prepare an amendment to defeat the
bill.
EUTHANASIA DOC TAKES ON PUBLICIST
A Northern Territory doctor who's been among the most vocal supporters of voluntary euthanasia has become so popular among the
world's media he's had to take on the services of a publicist.
Harry M. Miller has offered his services to Dr Phillip Nitshcke
free of charge to help the doctor organise the thousands of
requests he receives each week for interviews.
Mr Miller says he's agreed to help because he supports voluntary
euthanasia.
COLLINS REJECTS DONDAS DEFENCE
Northern Territory Labor Senator, Bob Collins, has rejected the
defence of Federal Member Nick Dondas of his vote on moving the
anti-euthanasia bill to a secondary chamber.
Mr Dondas says it would have been a serious tactical mistake to
vote against the government on a simple procedural matter of moving
the debate to a side chamber.
Mr Dondas says such a vote would have been seen by other members
who support the Territory, as obstructing the government's legislative program.
But Senator Collins says all Coalition members would have
recognised the political need for Mr Dondas - as the Territory's
sole member in the House of Representatives - to vote against the
move.
NEW LIBERAL DISCUSSION GROUP SET UP
Moderate members of the Federal Liberal party are being invited to
join a new discussion group.
South Australians Chris Gallus and Sue Jeanes and New South Wales
MP, Joe Hockey, are behind the group, named after the 19th Century philosopher, John Stuart Mill.
They've denied the group will become an informal faction, and say
it hasn't been set up as a rival to the more right wing Lyons
forum.
The first issue to be discussed by the group will be compulsory
voting, and Mr Hockey says it will also debate issues like regulating the Internet and Commonwealth-state relations.
NO MORE MONEY TO CHASE SKASE, SAYS GOVERNMENT
The Commonwealth has decided not to provide any more funding to
recover assets from former media tycoon, Christopher Skase.
A spokesperson for Federal Attorney General Darryl Williams says the decision was made by the Inspector General of the Insolvency
and Trustee Service.
To date, the Commonwealth has spent nearly 800-thousand dollars
pursuing Mr Skase.
In 1994 the former Labor Government failed to have Mr Skase extradited from Spain following legal action in a Spanish Court.
He was wanted in Australia to face company code charges.
